🌎 BEYOND THE 956

MIAMI, Fla. — An Arizona orthopedic surgeon was arrested October 20 at PortMiami after authorities allegedly found drugs — including MDMA, THC edibles and psychedelic chocolate bars — in his luggage as he prepared to board a cruise to the Bahamas, according to reports citing court documents and the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office.

Dr. Jacob Lee Henrichsen, 38, of Central, Arizona, was detained at Cruise Terminal B during a U.S. Customs and Border Protection luggage screening operation dubbed “Operation Temptation,” as he prepared to board Norwegian Cruise Line's Norwegian Jewel for a five-night adults-only sailing to Key West and Nassau, Bahamas.

According to the arrest report cited in multiple reports, officers allegedly found THC gummies, gummies, pills and capsules that tested positive for MDMA, a vape pen, lollipops, mints and mushroom-branded chocolate bars in his luggage. Henrichsen faces three felony charges, including one first-degree felony count of MDMA trafficking and two counts of possession of controlled substances.

Henrichsen, who practices at Mount Graham Regional Medical Center in Safford, Arizona, was released on a $10,000 bond, according to court summaries cited in reports. His attorney has entered a not-guilty plea on his behalf, requested a jury trial, and disputed how the alleged drug quantities were calculated.

Two other passengers boarding the same ship were also arrested separately on drug allegations during the same operation, and authorities have not indicated the cases were connected. Norwegian Cruise Line directed questions about the arrests to Customs and Border Protection.

Henrichsen has only been charged, not convicted. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post; The Arizona Republic (azcentral.com); Cruise News.

title: Beyond the 956: Arizona Surgeon Arrested at PortMiami on Drug Trafficking Charges Before Bahamas Cruise
